title: Develop a high energy proton beam position monitor using linear contact image sensor
author: Hsiao, Niu, et al.

steps.title: Assemble beamline and detector setup
steps.instruction: Produce a high‑energy proton beam with a cyclotron (model P235, SHI, Japan) and transport it through the beam line, exit window and air to the experimental bench; place the plastic scintillator (BC‑408, 100 × 100 × 3 mm, density 1.03 g cm⁻³) on the bench, cover it with a black sheet, position a 60‑mm‑thick copper block containing a 10‑mm‑diameter hole in front of the scintillator as a beam‑shape collimator, attach a linear contact image sensor (CIS) of ~187 mm length, 100 dpi (254 µm pixel) and scan speed <20 µs / line to the top edge of the scintillator, connect the CIS output to front‑end electronics (Cortex‑M3 RISC processor with 10‑bit ADC) that send data via a Raspberry Pi Model 3 B (1.2 GHz quad‑core ARM Cortex‑A53, 1 GB LPDDR2 RAM) to a PC, and affix an EBT3 film to the backside of the scintillator for reference imaging.

steps.title: Measure and set background threshold
steps.instruction: Place the assembled PS + CIS system in a dark box, record the background spectrum originating from CIS dark current, note the background level of 80 units, set the detection threshold to 80 units and shift all acquired data by 80 units, and limit the ADC readout range to 944 counts (max 10‑bit ADC = 1024).

steps.title: Configure ADC and acquisition settings
steps.instruction: Program the acquisition software so that each measurement lasts approximately 1 s, collects 726 data points per measurement, and allows up to 21 consecutive measurements; ensure the ADC operates with 10‑bit resolution and the custom limit of 944 counts.

steps.title: Acquire beam data at specified conditions
steps.instruction: Expose the PS + CIS detector to a proton beam of 230 MeV energy and 1 nA current for 21 seconds total (≈21 measurements of 1 s each) while recording the CIS signal; optionally repeat measurements at other beam currents (0.5 nA–1 nA) without the collimator for comparative studies.

steps.title: Analyze data and compute beam position
steps.instruction: For each 1‑s measurement, fit the 726‑point signal curve with a Gaussian function to obtain the mean (beam position) and standard deviation (beam size); report the mean peak position (41.99 mm) with a standard deviation of 30 µm, and compare the results with the EBT3 film exposure; note that signal height increases with beam intensity up to ~800 units before photodiode saturation and that the dynamic range for 230 MeV protons is approximately 0.5 nA–1 nA.
